h: The Mann Reveals the Life Within Torah

p: כָּל הַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם (דְּבָרִים ח, א)
"All the commandment that I command you today" (Devarim 8:1)
וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזֵר וּמַתְחִיל בִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד
Afterward it again begins in the singular,
that the words of Torah were essentially
just as the Ten Commandments were said
after there shone into the whole Jewish nation
the holiness of the Avos and the shepherds.
And that is why it says,
"All the commandment that I command you":
who shone into Yisrael from his level,
the aspect of the clear lens;
and this they will merit chiefly in the future.
This is alluded to in the word hayom, "today":
the heh indicates the upper heh,
which before was "a dalet that became,"
that the holiness be closed in the heart
which indicates the middah of Malchus,
the intent is that there shine
the holiness of the six middos
into the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
so that it will be forever.
And it says, "so that you will live":
it alludes to Mashiach ben Yosef,
who will conquer all the nations of the world
וְיוֹצִיא מֵהֶם כָּל הַי׳ קַבִּין חָכְמָה
and take out of them all the ten kavin of wisdom
along the lines of what it says (Nechemiah 9:6):
"And You give life to them all";
and this is the meaning of "so that you will live."
הוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד
corresponds to the aspect of Mashiach ben Dovid,
when they will merit much wisdom
Yehoshua would have been Mashiach ben Yosef,
and he would have conquered everything,
and Moshe Rabbeinu would then have shone forth
as it will be in the future,
along the lines of what they said (Koheles 1:9):
"And you shall remember the whole way," etc.,
"in the wilderness, in order to afflict you," etc.;
that is, in eating the mann,
which was considered an affliction for them,
"And He afflicted you and let you hunger,
and fed you the mann," etc.
And although they sensed in the mann
the taste of all kinds of foods,
nevertheless it was considered an affliction for them,
But in truth the eating of the mann was
so that the Torah would be
And that is why it says,
This is along the lines of how we explained
"But by My Name Hashem I did not make Myself known to them":
that it is the secret of Daas,
the level of Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
which the Avos did not merit;
the revelation of the Name Havayah,
they did not merit the secret of Daas
(and it was explained in Parashas Va'eira).
And the mann was the portion of Moshe Rabbeinu,
"The mann was in the merit of Moshe."
And that is why it says, "in order to make you know":
for the purpose of the mann
was to instill Daas in you.
that is, even with words of Torah,
when one merits "what comes forth from the mouth of Hashem"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רא, ב)
And certainly also on Erev Shabbos
and it was the middah called "the mouth of Hashem."
he would have tasted of the Tree of Life;
when the mixture of good and evil came about,
so that he would know to taste only of the good.
וְזֶה זָכָה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת
And this he merited through the holiness of Shabbos,
as written in the holy Zohar cited above.
And that is why it says,
כִּי עַל כָּל מוֹצָא פִי ה׳
"but by all that comes forth from the mouth of Hashem
"Your garment did not wear out upon you":
only the garments of the Torah,
that too "did not wear out upon you."
that is, even what one serves
the level of Moshe Rabbeinu and his holiness.
and that they be able to merit
when he will flow into them
from his level and his holiness,
so that each Jew will merit
in words of Torah from the root.
